content.body: `bool()` treats every non-empty string and object as true. A malformed value such as `"false"` therefore disables the bot-author and draft gates. This flag controls an approval security boundary, so invalid input must fail closed.
content.title: The privileged flag accepts non-boolean values
content.suggestion: Require a JSON boolean. Use `context.get("self_driving_review") is True`. Reject other present types if the caller needs a clear contract error.

content.body: The prompt renders `familiarity_block` before the self-driving provenance block. A self-driving classification can still contain familiarity data. The prompt then presents author history as trusted evidence while also saying that this history carries no signal. This breaks the stated trust contract and can bias the review of machine-authored code.
content.title: The prompt does not enforce removal of author familiarity
content.suggestion: Do not render familiarity when `cl.get("self_driving")` is true. Enforce this in `_build_review_prompt` so every caller gets the same security invariant.

content.body: The deferred import runs before the try block. An import error will escape the on-commit callback. The caller can then report a failure after the database commit succeeds.
content.title: Deferred import can escape the error handler
content.suggestion: Move the `queue_inbox_pr_review` import inside the try block. This keeps all dispatch failures within the documented fire-and-forget boundary.

content.body: The row lock does not serialize calls when no matching ReviewRun exists. Concurrent receiver tasks can both create runs and start costly workflows for one head.
content.title: Concurrent receiver tasks can create duplicate reviews
content.suggestion: Add a database uniqueness constraint for pull_request and head_sha. Catch IntegrityError and restart or reuse the winning run, as the webhook path does.

content.body: The Celery publish is the only handoff for the initial review. The caller catches publish failures, so a broker outage can lose the review permanently.
content.title: A broker failure permanently loses the initial review
content.suggestion: Use a durable outbox or a persisted dispatch state with retries. Do not depend on another TaskRun save to repeat the publish.

content.body: The carve-out accepts every GitHub bot. It can also identify a run by its branch when the run has no saved PR URL. An unrelated bot can create a repository-native PR with the same branch name. This match bypasses the draft, author, review mode, and write-permission gates. StampHog can then approve a PR that the implementation run did not create.
content.title: Branch fallback can authorize a PR from an unrelated bot
content.suggestion: Require an exact saved PR URL before this code grants the carve-out. If the branch fallback must remain, verify the expected PostHog Code bot identity and bind the fetched PR URL to the TaskRun before review.

content.body: The document says that both trigger paths verify task linkage before they set `ReviewRun.output["inbox_review"]`. The webhook path calls `find_signal_implementation_run`, but `process_inbox_pr_review` trusts its IDs. It does not load `task_run_id` or verify its team, signal report, repository, or PR. A new caller of the public facade can therefore mark an unrelated bot draft as trusted self-driving work. This mark bypasses the bot, draft, review-mode, and author-permission gates.
content.title: Initial review path does not verify the documented task linkage
content.suggestion: Make `process_inbox_pr_review` load the task run through the tasks facade. Verify the team, signal report, repository, and PR URL before it creates the review run. Alternatively, change the document so it does not claim that the initial path verifies this linkage, but that leaves a weak trust boundary.

content.body: The task trusts `team_id`, `task_run_id`, `signal_report_id`, `acting_user_id`, and `pr_url`. It only checks for a repository configuration and an open PR. A forged or stale call can mark any open PR in that repository as an inbox review. This mark bypasses the bot, draft, review mode, and author permission gates. An untrusted task agent can also record an unrelated PR URL in its output. The resulting run can post an approval to code that did not come from the claimed implementation run.
content.title: Initial review trusts unverified task provenance
content.suggestion: Load the `TaskRun` by `task_run_id` and `team_id` before the GitHub request. Check its signal report, repository, non-internal status, and saved PR URL. Resolve the acting reviewer and toggle again. After the GitHub request, require the expected bot author and a repository-native head. Create the inbox provenance only after all checks pass.

content.body: `find_task_run` searches all teams and selects one row before this facade checks `team_id`. Two teams can have tasks for the same repository, PR URL, or branch. A row from another team can win the query and cause this function to return `None`, even when the requested team has a valid run. This does not implement the documented team-scoped lookup contract.
content.title: Team scope is applied after an unscoped run selection
content.suggestion: Apply `team_id` inside the query before `.first()`. For example, add an optional `team_id` argument to `find_task_run` and filter `TaskRun.objects` with it in each lookup path. Keep the final team check as a fail-closed guard.

content.body: The PR requires a Stamphog review when any assigned reviewer opts in. This code selects one acting reviewer before it checks the toggle. If the task creator or first reviewer opts out, the code skips the review even when another assigned reviewer opts in.
content.title: The toggle check ignores other assigned reviewers
content.suggestion: Resolve all assigned reviewers for the Stamphog gate. Select an opted-in reviewer from that set. Keep the task creator as the first choice when that user opts in. Use the same selection rule in resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer so initial reviews and webhook reviews agree.

content.body: The task trusts the `acting_user_id` selected before the Celery message was published. A user can disable inbox reviews while the message waits in the queue. The delayed task still creates a review with self-driving provenance.
content.title: The queued task does not recheck the review toggle
content.suggestion: Resolve the acting reviewer again immediately before run creation. Use the registered resolver with the verified signal report and task creator. Stop when the resolver returns `None`, and store the newly resolved user ID in the provenance.

A durable outbox table plus a relay would be a new subsystem to close a sub-second-to-minutes broker-outage window in a brand-new, per-user-toggle-gated experimental feature.

That is a narrow, self-healing window, and the suggested fix is disproportionate infrastructure for it — overengineering against a rare edge case, per the validation bar.

This is PostHog-internal infrastructure, so the pool of who could exploit it is limited to org members/apps on an opted-in repo — real but not internet-facing, so `should_fix` rather than `must_fix`.

- **Checked:** The flagged receiver leg `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1230), its only caller `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155) and the review_hog receiver that fires it (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-141), the provenance consumption `self_driving_review` (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451, products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:113-131), and the approval posting path (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:723-756).

It is not one: `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)` is reachable only from inside the deployment (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149), and a caller with broker access can already enqueue ANY task with ANY args — re-verifying args inside this one task adds no protection against that attacker. That half is defensive-coding paranoia against trusted infrastructure.
- **Found:** The 'agent records an unrelated PR URL' half is partially accurate on mechanics: `process_inbox_pr_review` indeed never loads the `TaskRun`, never checks the PR author is the team's App bot, and never checks a repo-native head (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1130-1230) — unlike the webhook carve-out, which does all three (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-186). A run created this way does stamp `inbox_review` provenance, which flips `self_driving_review=True` and waives the engine's bot/draft refusal (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451, products/stamphog/backend/logic/reviewer.py:113-117), and an APPROVE verdict posts a real GitHub approval (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:745).

The task no-ops unless the PR's repository has a synced+enabled `StamphogRepoConfig` for the given `team_id` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1153) — i.e. only the team's own connected repos, the same repos the agent already has push access to (it opened its own PR there). A malicious or prompt-injected agent capable of writing a foreign `pr_url` into its output could equally push the same commits to its own PR branch, which the system would legitimately review and approve — the claimed escalation adds no capability the agent lacks.
- **Found:** The trust placed in agent-written `output.pr_url` is also the pre-existing, deliberate contract: the same receiver fires the whole ReviewHog workflow off the identical field with no re-verification (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:115-125), and the tasks webhook backstop persists agent-observed PR URLs (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:203-225). The PR follows the established trust boundary rather than weakening it.

Does not meet the bar for a real, reachable security problem.

- **Checked:** The flagged facade `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516), the matcher it delegates to `find_task_run` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:29-98), the `TaskRun.branch` field (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1081), and the consuming carve-out (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:191-200).
- **Found:** The claim is mechanically correct. `find_task_run` queries `TaskRun.objects` with NO team filter in every leg: pr_url (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:41), branch (lines 68-76), wizard head branch (lines 85-93) — then `.first()` picks one row. `find_signal_implementation_run` only afterwards discards the winner when `run.team_id != team_id` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:505) and returns `None`, without ever looking for the requested team's own matching run.
- **Found:** Cross-team collision is realistic, not hypothetical: `TaskRun.branch` is a free-form, caller-supplied string (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1081, no uniqueness), and `Task.repository` is likewise unconstrained — two PostHog teams can both run implementation tasks against the same GitHub repository, and branch names like `main`-adjacent or conventional `fix/...` names collide. The branch leg's queryset has no ORDER BY (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:68-76), so which team's row wins `.first()` is arbitrary. The pre-existing comment in the same function already acknowledges cross-repo branch collisions (lines 61-63) — the same hazard exists cross-team.
- **Found:** The consequence is a silently lost re-review, fail-closed: when another team's row shadows the match, the carve-out resolves empty (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:199-200) and the self-driving PR is treated as a plain bot draft — the PR's own Case 2 (re-review on new commits) never runs. No approval leaks to the wrong team (the `run.team_id != repo_config.team_id` recheck holds), so this is a correctness bug against the documented contract — 'answers only for the self-driving shape... team scoping is enforced here' (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:491-495) — not a security hole.
- **Impact:** Missed reviews in exactly the multi-team-same-repo dogfooding setup this feature targets. The fix is small (thread `team_id` into `find_task_run`'s filters, keeping the post-check as fail-closed guard), matching how other facade functions already take `team_id` (e.g. `get_task_run`, products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:473-476).

- **Checked:** The flagged provenance block (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1176-1181), the publish-time toggle gate in the receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:114-139), what `acting_user_id` actually drives downstream (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451, 745), and the retry profile of the task (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109, 1162-1165).
- **Found:** The toggle is re-checked fresh at EVERY publish: `handle_task_run_saved` loads `ReviewUserSettings` and requires `settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` in the same save handling that enqueues the task, on every TaskRun save that refires the receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:114-139). The only un-gated span is broker latency between publish and execution — seconds normally, minutes at worst under retries (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109).
- **Found:** `acting_user_id` is attribution-only on this leg. The review posts as the stamphog GitHub App under the installation token (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:660, 745); the provenance dict feeds analytics segmentation and UI labeling (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:175-176), not any authorization decision. A stale value grants nothing the toggle-off user could not have received moments earlier.
- **Found:** The asymmetry with the webhook leg is deliberate, not an oversight: the webhook path re-resolves the toggle per delivery (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:201-205) because each webhook event is a new trigger arriving arbitrarily long after opt-in — hours or days later. The receiver leg's opt-in check happens in the same request that publishes the task; the race the issue describes needs the user to disable the setting inside a seconds-to-minutes queue window, and the consequence is one review of their own agent's draft PR — code that IS reviewed, head-pinned, and retracted by the opted-out dismissal path on the next push (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:894-898).
- **Found:** Re-resolving inside the task is also not free of its own semantics: the resolver re-derives the acting reviewer from the report's LATEST suggested_reviewers artefact (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:159-207), so a mid-queue artefact update could silently swap the governing reviewer — the publish-time value is the canonical resolution the receiver already made.
- **Impact:** A preference-staleness race with a seconds-to-minutes window whose worst case is one automated review of reviewed code on the team's own PR — rare, low-impact, self-limiting. This does not meet the bar for a correctness bug that real inputs will hit; it is a theoretical timing edge on a user preference, not a safety or trust boundary.

- **Checked:** products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:111-139 (TaskRun trigger), receivers.py:144-156 (`resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`), receivers.py:159-207 (`_resolve_assigned_reviewer`), products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:195-215 (webhook leg consuming the registered resolver), products/stamphog/backend/facade/inbox_hooks.py:20-33 (hook contract).
- **Found:** `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (receivers.py:206) collapses the full resolved reviewer set to exactly one user: the task creator if assigned, else `resolved[0]`. Both toggle checks then read only that one user's settings: `settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` at receivers.py:126 (initial review) and receivers.py:154 (webhook re-review). If the picked user has the toggle off, both paths return without checking any other assigned reviewer.
- **Found:** The single-user gate directly contradicts the feature's own stated contract. The PR description says the review runs when "at least one of the assigned users has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled," and Case 3 says "nobody is opted in, so no review runs" — both describe an any-reviewer opt-in, not a single-reviewer one.
- **Found:** The concrete failure: user A (toggle on) and user B (toggle off) are both assigned reviewers; the task creator is not in the assigned set and B sorts first in `resolved` (or B is the creator). The Stamphog review never runs despite A opting in. The same selection is used in `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`, so the webhook leg agrees with the initial leg — the bug is consistent, not a divergence, and the suggestion's demand for a shared selection rule is already structurally satisfied.
- **Impact:** A user who explicitly opted in to Stamphog reviews gets silently no reviews whenever a non-opted-in reviewer wins the deterministic first slot — a realistic multi-reviewer assignment, not a contrived edge case. Wrong gating outcome on the feature's core toggle = correctness bug; it also contradicts the feature's documented behavior.
- **Priority:** Keeping `must_fix` — the gate fails for the primary use case the PR ships (any assigned reviewer opting in should trigger the review) and the fix (scan the resolved set for an opted-in reviewer, preferring the creator) is small and local.
